headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks: Devin’s broad write/network autonomy can ingest or act on ComfyUI outputs, while shared workspace/integration paths create conflict and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between ComfyUI and Devin, so prompt injection is not default. However, Devin can read files and use MCP, while ComfyUI exposes files and a Comfy API; if outputs are manually bridged or placed in shared files, attacker-controlled content could be misread as instructions. The pathway is weaker than default but plausible.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into a Devin-readable workspace file
IF Devin is connected to an MCP server or integration that forwards ComfyUI artifacts without provenance
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory not mounted into Devin
Disable MCP/integration paths for any folder receiving generated artifacts
Use a manual review step before Devin consumes image/workflow text
Prefix bridged artifacts with a non-executable metadata header
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts, while Devin reads files, writes files, and sends data to broad third-party APIs. If both share a workspace or repo clone, Devin can ingest ComfyUI-generated assets and transmit them through integrations. The leakage path exists in common setups and is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF ComfyUI and Devin share a filesystem or repo clone
IF generated media or workflow files contain sensitive content
IF Devin forwards workspace contents to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or MCP
mitigations: Separate the storage locations for generated media and coding work
Restrict Devin integrations for any project containing sensitive assets
Review and redact ComfyUI outputs before handing them to Devin
Turn off automatic sync from shared folders to external services
requires-engineering: enforce per-project data classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git, and broad network access; ComfyUI can also operate on files and runs asynchronously. If both touch the same directory or repo, Devin can overwrite models, workflows, or outputs while ComfyUI is active, causing destructive conflicts. The pair’s default autonomy makes this dangerous without explicit coordination.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo clone
IF ComfyUI model/workflow files are mutable during Devin edits
IF Devin commits or rewrites files while ComfyUI is running
mitigations: Use separate directories for models and code
Pause ComfyUI before Devin edits shared files
Lock the repo or workspace during Devin write operations
Keep Devin off any directory containing checkpoints or workflows
requires-engineering: add file-locking or lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a planner-executor that can act autonomously with shell, browser, and write permissions, so it may treat ComfyUI outputs as authoritative if they are handed over as artifacts or text. ComfyUI can generate workflows and assets that Devin could then commit, message, or deploy without verification. That creates a default cascade from generation to action with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF Devin consumes ComfyUI outputs as task inputs or evidence
IF no human or automated verification step checks those outputs
IF Devin is allowed to commit, message, or deploy based on them
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on ComfyUI outputs
Add a verification checklist for any generated artifact
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for tasks sourced from ComfyUI
Log and diff all downstream actions triggered by generated content
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is open-source and offline-capable, while Devin is closed-source, cloud-hosted, and handles repo deploy keys plus integration tokens. If regulated or sensitive media is processed, Devin’s vendor-managed workspace and broad integrations can create residency or retention mismatches. The compliance risk is real in default cloud workflows, though not enough evidence for a higher rating.
conditions: IF sensitive media or secrets are placed into Devin’s cloud workspace
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing or specific residency
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to artifacts copied from ComfyUI
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin’s workspace
Use ComfyUI offline for sensitive generation tasks
Review Devin retention and deletion settings before use
Avoid storing secrets in shared project artifacts
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review for the workflow
